verdicts.quote: If the import ends `rejected` for any file-level or row-level error, no user from that file exists, including the rows that were valid
for `rejected`, the total number of errors and every error entry (row, column, reason code, message)

every later row with the same address gets an error for column `email` with reason `duplicate_in_file` … equals that of any existing user, in state `invited`, `active` or `deactivated`, gets an error for column `email` with reason `already_exists`
Admin rights are checked again when the users are about to be created … Roles are `member` or `admin`; empty means `member` … These are the only two roles an import can assign.
Active admins can use the import page and submit a CSV … Everyone else is refused with HTTP 403 on every import-related request
verdicts.missing: The spec identifies eligible importers but leaves the relationship between permission to create one user and permission to bulk-import unstated.

verdicts.quote: The first record that is not blank is the header. … the header lacks `email` or lacks `name` (or lacks both), the import ends `rejected` … Unrecognised columns are ignored and reported
A leading byte-order mark is ignored … a field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas, doubled double quotes (`""` for one `"`) and line breaks. Records end with LF or CRLF
When an import becomes `succeeded`, each of its users is sent one email at the address in the file, not before the users exist and never for `rejected` or `failed` imports.
A file with 5,000 data rows is accepted for validation; a file with 5,001 or more data rows ends `rejected` with file-level reason `too_many_rows`
An empty file is refused … A header without data is refused … When no error exists, the number of users created equals the number of data rows read, each row producing exactly one user

a further upload by the same admin is refused with reason `import_in_progress` … Uploading a file whose users were created by an earlier import ends `rejected` with `already_exists` on every row, "0 users created"
the upload must not depend on a single web request lasting as long as processing. … watches the status change without reloading, or closes the page and later opens the import history.
One invitation email per created user, sent only after success … Under normal operation each invitation of an import reaches delivery `sent` or `failed` within 1 hour
verdicts.missing: A builder must decide whether to send all invitations at once or spread them out, and at what rate.

verdicts.quote: starts as `invited` … No passwords are taken from the file … They open the link within 7 days, choose a password, and their status becomes `active`; they can then sign in with that email address and password.
The uploaded file is not kept after processing … Once an import reaches a final status, no page or address offers the original uploaded file for download.
verdicts.missing: The spec leaves the storage location and who, if anyone, can download the original while the import is queued or processing undecided.

verdicts.quote: the file name, the uploading admin and the upload time … for `succeeded`, the list of the users created (email, name, role, and each one's invitation delivery)
The admin fixes rows 17 and 42 in the file, uploads it again … all-or-nothing makes re-uploading a corrected file safe
verdicts.missing: The spec describes a whole-file retry. It leaves cancellation during processing and any separate retry action for just the failed rows unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Under normal load, an import of 5,000 valid rows goes from upload to `succeeded` within 60 seconds. … the shown status is refreshed without the admin reloading, at intervals of 5 seconds or less
by hand in user management … No import changes, deactivates, re-roles, renames, re-invites or deletes any user who existed when it was accepted
verdicts.missing: The spec recognizes manual creation and protects existing users, but leaves open whether adding import may change the existing manual creation flow or its validation behavior.
